name: Total Abdominal Hysterectomy with Bilateral Salpingo-oophorectomy
overview: Removal of uterus, cervix, fallopian tubes, and ovaries

pimpingQuestions.question: The uterus develops from fusion of which embryologic ducts?
pimpingQuestions.answer: The paramesonephric (Mullerian) ducts — bilateral ducts fuse caudally to form the uterus, cervix, and upper vagina. The unfused cranial portions become the fallopian tubes. Failure of fusion: bicornuate uterus, septate uterus, uterus didelphys. The Mullerian ducts require absence of AMH (anti-Mullerian hormone) to develop — in males, AMH causes their regression.

pimpingQuestions.question: What are the key ligaments divided during TAH-BSO?
pimpingQuestions.answer: 1) Round ligament (first divided), 2) Infundibulopelvic (IP) ligament (contains ovarian artery and vein — for BSO), 3) Utero-ovarian ligament (if ovaries preserved), 4) Broad ligament (peritoneal fold), 5) Cardinal (Mackenrodt's) ligament (main uterine support — contains uterine artery), 6) Uterosacral ligaments (posterior support).

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the blood supply to the uterus, and where does the ureter cross the uterine artery?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Uterine artery (from internal iliac) — the main supply. The ureter crosses UNDER the uterine artery at the level of the cervix ('water under the bridge') — this is the most common site of ureteral injury during hysterectomy (1-2% incidence). Also: ovarian artery (from aorta) supplies via the IP ligament.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the most common complication of TAH-BSO?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Surgical site infection (5-10%) including wound infection and vaginal cuff cellulitis. Ureteral injury (1-2%), bladder injury (0.5-1%), hemorrhage requiring transfusion (2-5%), and vaginal cuff dehiscence (<1%). Prophylactic antibiotics (single-dose cefazolin) reduce SSI by 50%.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the current recommendation for opportunistic salpingectomy during hysterectomy?
pimpingQuestions.answer: The Society of Gynecologic Oncology (SGO) recommends bilateral salpingectomy at the time of hysterectomy for benign disease (even if ovaries are preserved) because high-grade serous ovarian cancers frequently originate from the fallopian tube fimbria (serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma, STIC). Removing tubes reduces ovarian cancer risk by 40-60% without affecting ovarian function.
